incidents.vector: Lateral movement to a senior finance executive's workstation planted two implants disguised as Adobe and OneDrive, used a legitimate Aspose .NET library to convert Outlook mail to local files, and exfiltrated via a Dropbox C2 channel.
incidents.impact: Five-plus months of near-continuous mailbox access (Aug 2025–Feb 17, 2026) yielded the executive's full inbox repeatedly, including non-public listings, enforcement, and market-moving deal data. Attackers lost access by mid-March 2026.

incidents.vector: Kinetic missile and drone barrage of about 30 projectiles struck the passenger terminal and a nearby military base; included in this brief because it disrupted civil-aviation IT and operations.
incidents.impact: All flights suspended and diverted to alternate airports; heavy damage to a passenger terminal; the worst attack on Kuwait since the April 8 Iran ceasefire.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of Google-verified ads from shell companies pushed Flutter-built fake desktop apps (PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, PDF-Ninja) signed with valid Apple Developer IDs and Apple-notarized; a WebView JavaScript-to-native bridge fetches the malicious logic from attacker servers at runtime.
incidents.impact: Backdoor (FlutterShell) provides shell command execution, file system manipulation, environment-variable theft, and AI-summarization-based data exfiltration; also hijacks Chrome to route traffic through ad-laden intermediaries. Zero VirusTotal detections at time of analysis; Google has since suspended the advertiser accounts.

incidents.victim: US and Israeli personnel and infrastructure (Iran MOIS 'Handala' physical-threat expansion)
incidents.vector: MOIS expanded its existing Handala hacktivist brand to include a new Handala Popular Resistance Front (HPRF) and three influence-operations personas that use Telegram channels to solicit physical attacks, assassinations, espionage, and sabotage in exchange for Bitcoin payments.
incidents.impact: Cyber-enabled physical threats targeting US and Israeli law enforcement, military, intelligence, energy, transportation, and research personnel; centralized brand amplifies recruitment reach and lowers attribution friction for state-directed violent operations.

incidents.victim: Red Hat (@redhat-cloud-services npm packages, ~117K weekly downloads)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply-chain worm operators (Mini Shai-Hulud / Miasma; attribution to TeamPCP uncertain after public source release)
incidents.vector: Compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account pushed malicious orphan commits that triggered the legitimate GitHub Actions OIDC publishing workflow, producing 32 Trojanized packages signed with valid SLSA provenance. A weaponized npm preinstall hook then detonated a 4.29 MB obfuscated dropper that downloaded the Bun runtime to execute a credential harvester.
incidents.impact: Stole GitHub, npm, AWS, Azure, GCP, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes, SSH, CI, browser, and wallet secrets; scraped GitHub Actions runner memory; installed passwordless sudo; republished poisoned packages from compromised maintainers; carried a destructive 'rm -rf ~/' tripwire. Red Hat removed the packages and npm hardened the namespace.

incidents.victim: Obama White House and US Space Force Chief Master Sergeant Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Telegram-shared exploit tricked Meta's AI customer-support chatbot into adding an attacker-controlled email to a target account during a password-reset flow (using a VPN exit matching the target's hometown), causing the bot to send a one-time reset code to the attacker.
incidents.impact: Accounts defaced with pro-Iranian imagery and messaging; pro-Iran hackers claimed to have hijacked multiple short, high-value Instagram handles. Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; surfaced when Charter's name was listed on ShinyHunters' dark-web leak portal.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a security breach after the extortion listing; scope of stolen data not yet disclosed publicly.

incidents.vector: Compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access the land and real-estate database.
incidents.impact: Approximately 600,000 records stolen, including real names, cadastral information, and other real-estate-specific details.

Hackers stole medical data plus biometric information — including fingerprints and palm prints — on at least 1.8 million people. The biometric exposure is particularly sensitive because affected individuals cannot replace those identifiers.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protection and published 844 MB of agency material to a public GitHub profile ('Private-CISA') used as a working scratchpad since November 2025.
incidents.impact: Plaintext credentials to dozens of internal CISA systems exposed, including AWS GovCloud keys and an RSA private key granting full access to every repository in the CISA-IT GitHub organization. More than a week after notification, several keys remained un-rotated; Congress has demanded answers.
